ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 15 V DC power supply marked with + and -; from the positive terminal it passes through thyristor T, then through inductor L, to capacitor C on the right side, and finally returns to the negative terminal of the power supply. Therefore T, L, C form a series branch and are connected across the 15 V power supply. Reasoning: The trigger pulse makes the originally off thyristor T conduct, equivalent to applying a 15 V step to a series LC circuit with initial voltage zero. The series LC current is i(t) = (15/Z0) sin(t/sqrt(LC)), where Z0 = sqrt(L/C). The thyristor maintains conduction when the current is positive; because the given latching current and holding current are both zero, it will turn off when the current first returns to zero after conduction. The first zero point satisfies t/sqrt(LC) = pi, so the conduction time t = pi sqrt(LC). Substituting L = (100/pi) μH, C = (100/pi) μF, gives sqrt(LC) = (100/pi) μs, therefore t = pi × (100/pi) μs = 100 μs. The 10 μs gate pulse width is shorter than this time, but under the assumption that the latching and holding currents are both zero, it does not change the conduction duration.

method.method_draft: After noting from the image that T, L, and C are in series across the 15 V source, model turn-on at the gate pulse as applying a 15 V step to an initially uncharged series LC. Write the series-LC current response i(t) = (15/Z0) sin(t/sqrt(LC)). The thyristor conducts while this current is positive and turns off at the first zero after turn-on, t = pi sqrt(LC). Substitute L = (100/pi) microH and C = (100/pi) microF, giving sqrt(LC) = (100/pi) microseconds, so t = 100 microseconds. Check that the 10 us pulse is shorter but irrelevant because latching and holding currents are zero.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, treat T as a switch that connects the uncharged capacitor and inductor in series to the 15 V supply when triggered. Use the resonant-charging fact that the current begins at zero, rises, and returns to zero when the capacitor has completed the first half-cycle of the LC oscillation. Thus the conduction interval is one half of the natural period: Tcond = T0/2 = pi sqrt(LC). With L and C both equal to 100/pi in micro-units, sqrt(LC) = 100/pi microseconds, hence Tcond = 100 microseconds. The 10 us gate pulse only initiates conduction; zero latching current lets conduction persist after the gate pulse ends.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个串联电路，左侧为 15 V 直流电源，上端标正、下端标负；上方支路从电源正端依次接有晶闸管 T、 电感 L，右侧再接电容 C 回到电源负端。电容初始未充电，晶闸管初始关断，触发后可把 L 和 C 串联接到 15 V 电源上。

推理：按题设和图中连接，触发晶闸管后可把 T 视为闭合开关，未充电电容 C 通过串联电感 L 进行谐振充电。LC 串联回路中电流从 0 开始上升，经过第一个半个自然周期后又回到 0；晶闸管的保持电流为 0，因此电流第一次回到 0 时关断。所以导通时间为半个 LC 自然周期：T_cond = T0/2 = π√(LC)。已知 L = (100/π) μH，C = (100/π) μF，因此 √(LC) = (100/π) μs。于是 T_cond = π × (100/π) μs = 100 μs。10 μs 的门极脉冲只用于启动导通；由于锁定电流为 0，脉冲结束后晶闸管仍可继续导通直到回路电流降为 0。
